JUDGMENT SHEET
IN THE LAHORE HIGH COURT, LAHORE
JUDICIAL DEPARTMENT
MUHAMMAD WAHEED KHAN, J.- This judgment shall
decide the instant appeal (Cr. Appeal No.34522 of 2025) filed by appellant,
Abdul Waheed (against his conviction and sentence) and Cr. Revision
No.41722 of 2025 filed by complainant, Ali Shan, for enhancement of
sentence of respondent No.1/appellant as both the matters have arisen out of
the same judgment dated 29.04.2025 passed by the learned Addl. Sessions
Judge, Nankana Sahib, in private complaint u/s 302, 148, 149 PPC arising
out of case FIR No.235/2023 at Police Station Baraghar, District Nankana
Sahib, whereby the appellant was convicted under Section 302(c) PPC and
sentenced to seven years rigorous imprisonment alongwith fine of
Rs.50,000/-, in default thereof, to further undergo six months simple
imprisonment. He was also held liable to pay compensation of Rs.2,00,000/-
to the legal heirs of deceased Mujahid Hussain as provided under section
544-A Cr.P.C. which shall be recoverable as arrears of land revenue and in
case of non-payment, to further undergo six months simple imprisonment.
Benefit u/s 382-B Cr.P.C. was also extended to him.
Cr. Appeal No.34522 of 2025
Abdul Waheed v. The State, etc.
Crl. Rev. No.41722 of 2025
Ali Shan v. Abdul Waheed etc.
JUDGMENT
body: Date of hearing 12.11.2026 Appellant by Mian Tabassum Ali, Advocate.
Complainant by Nemo.
State by Mr. Muhammad Waqas Anwar, DPG.
Whereas five co-accused persons, Waleed, Muhammad Yasir, Muhammad Faisal, Abdul Majeed and Rehana Kausar, were acquitted from the case vide the same judgment.

2. Brief facts of the case as narrated by the complainant Ali Shah in private complaint (Ex-PB) are that:- “He was a driver of loader mazda and his father had died 19/20 years ago. He and his three brothers and one sister are married and are residing in the same house, his elder brother Dilawar Hussain had gone abroad (Saudi Arabia) in connection with labour, his brother Mujahid Hussain was a driver of a school van, who had his daughter, ‘Areej’, 3/4. On 07.04.2023, he along with his family was present in his house, when accused Faisal and Waleed sons of Abdul Waheed residents of the same vicinity called his brother Mujahid for work and when his brother did not came back for sufficient time, then the complainant along with his cousin Muhammad Attique and Abdul Rehman went out to find out their brother Mujahid Hussain and when reached near the house of accused Faisal, they on hearing noise, entered the house and saw in the light of electric bulb that accused Faisal armed with 12 bore gun, Waleed armed with sota, Yasir armed with pistol, Abdul Waheed armed with sota and two unknown accused were beating his brother and in their view accused Faisal fired with 12 bore gun, which hit on different parts of body of his brother, whereas Yasir also fired pistol shots, upon which his brother fell down and succumbed to the wounds and the accused persons fled away. Motive behind the occurrence was that accused persons had suspicion that Mujahid Hussain had illicit relations with their sister Memona 22/23 and due to this grudge, they had murdered Mujahid Hussain with their consultation”.

3. After registration of case, matter was investigated by the police, but being dis-satisfied with the investigation, the complainant filed a private complaint, in which the appellant along with others was summoned to face trial by the learned trial Court. Thereafter, formal charge was framed against him, to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. The prosecution in order to prove its case produced as many as three PWs and nine CWs. Ocular account was furnished by complainant Ali Shan (PW-1) and Abdul Rehman (PW-2). Evidence of extra judicial confession was tendered by Ehsan Elahi (PW-3). Medical evidence was furnished by Dr. Muhammad Arslan Munir (CW-4), who conducted postmortem examination on the dead body of the deceased. Investigation of the case was carried out by Manzoor Ahmad SI (CW-9) and Allah Wasaya Inspector (CW-12), whereas the remaining witnesses were formal in nature and after producing certain documents closed its evidence. After completion of prosecution evidence, statement of the appellant was recorded u/s 342 Cr.P.C., in which he denied all the allegations leveled against him by the prosecution. He opted not to appear as his own witness u/s 340 (2) Cr.P.C., however produced certain documents in his defence evidence. After evaluating prosecution evidence available on record, learned trial Court found the prosecution version correct beyond any shadow of doubt, resulted into conviction and sentence of the appellant in the afore stated terms.

4. In support of the instant appeal, learned counsel for the appellant contends that case of the prosecution is inherently flawed, hence, fails to inspire confidence; that witnesses of the ocular account were closely related to the deceased, so, being interested witnesses, their testimonies cannot be believed to maintain conviction of the appellant and even otherwise, both the PWs have also failed to advance any plausible reason qua their availability at the crime scene at the relevant time of the alleged incident, so, no implicit reliance can be made on their evidence, specially under the circumstances when their evidence was disbelieved to the extent of acquitted co-accused, who were also ascribed active role while committing the crime; that the defence plea taken by the appellant was believed by the learned trial Court to some extent but despite this factum, the appellant was convicted; that medical evidence was not in line with ocular account; that nothing incriminating material was recovered from possession of the appellant; that motive set up by the prosecution remained unproved; that the impugned judgment is based on surmises and conjectures as material evidence available on record in favour of the appellant has been mis-read by the learned trial Court and lastly prays that since the prosecution has miserably failed to prove its case against the appellant up to hilt, hence, by accepting the instant appeal, he be acquitted of the charge.

5. Conversely, learned Deputy Prosecutor General has faithfully defended the impugned judgment by controverting the arguments of learned counsel for the appellant and has contended that the prosecution has ably proved its case against the appellant “beyond reasonable shadow of doubt”; that the prosecution has also produced two witnesses of the ocular account, who gave plausible reason qua their availability at the crime scene at the time of alleged incident, thus their presence at the crime scene cannot be doubted at any hypotheses; that medical evidence also corroborates the ocular account, which was also duly supported by the evidence of recovery of weapon of offence and evidence of motive, so, in presence of voluminous evidence, the appellant does not deserve any leniency and he has rightly been adjudged guilty by the learned trial Court, hence, the instant appeal is liable to be dismissed and the appellant be convicted in accordance with law as provided in such like offences.

6. I have heard arguments of learned counsel for the appellant, learned Law Officer and have perused the record with their assistance. At the very outset, it is observed that since the learned trial Court itself, discarded the eye witness account furnished by complainant Ali Shan (PW-1) and Abdul Rehman (PW-2) and their presence at the crime scene was found highly doubtful and not worthy of credence. Apart from the fact that their testimonies were incompatible with the facts and attending circumstances of the case, learned trial Court in paragraph No.27 of the impugned judgment has unambiguously declared that no conviction can be awarded on the basis of such evidence. However, while relying on the statement of the appellant and other five co-accused (since acquitted), learned trial Court convicted and sentence the appellant by holding that he had ‘exaggerated the right of self defence’. So, in that eventuality, there is no need to discuss the credibility and sanctity of the eye witness account as on going through the impugned judgment, I am also in agreement with the findings and reasons mentioned therein qua discrediting the same. Case of the appellant since inception has been that on the fateful night, brother of complainant, Mujahid Hussain (deceased) had entered his house with illicit intention and subjected his unmarried daughter, Memona, to rape and when on hearing hue and cry, he (complainant) and his sons attracted to the room of Memona Bibi, they saw that Mujahid Hussain (deceased) was having firearm weapon/revolver in his hand and had sexually assaulted daughter of the appellant. While answering to question No.20 (Why this case made against you and why the PWs deposed against you?), the appellant replied as under;- “I have four sons namely Waleed, Faisal and Yasir who are normal persons whereas, Naveed is a special person. I had only one daughter namely Memoona Bibi. My house is situated in the center of village Abaadi. 10/12 other houses are also located in the line of street of houses alongwith my house. My house is situated at a distance of about 6 acres from the house of complainant and the deceased. On the date of occurrence, it was month of Holy Ramzan. At about midnight time I heard the hue and cry of my daughter upon which I awoked up alongwith other family members and when came towards the room of my daughter we saw deceased Mujahid Hussain was having firearm weapon/revolver in his hand who had committed rape with my daughter on gun point; that due to this fact I picked up my licensed pump action gun; that in the meanwhile deceased Mujahid Hussain came in the veranda from the room and he aimed his firearm weapon towards me and upon impending danger and out of grave and sudden provocation due to act of accused I made firing upon his person who became injured and later-on succumbed to the injuries at the spot. At that time he was not wearing any kameez upon his body. After the occurrence I made call to the police upon police rescue 15, police reached there, inspected the spot in which Mujahid Hussain committed the rape with my daughter inspected the dead body of deceased and also inquired from myself, my daughter Memoona Bibi, my wife Rehana Bibi and my son co-accused Waleed. My Sons Faisal and Yasir were not present at the place of occurrence at the time of occurrence. Faisal was in his cattle-shed which was 2/3 acres away from my house/place of occurrence, whereas, Yasir co-accused was in the house of his in laws in chak No.99/GB Tehsil Jaranwala District Faisalabad. After conducting inquiry at the place of occurrence, the police summoned the complainant from his house who came there alongwith his witnesses Attique and Abdul Rehman. Police then shifted the dead body of the deceased to police station and also took me, my sons Waleed and Faisal as well as my daughter Memoona to the police station. I also handed over my licensed pump action to the police then and there which was also taken into possession by the police and later-on a bogus recovery of said weapon was shown in police investigation against me. This occurrence took place due to blameworthy conduct of deceased as he trespassed/intruded into our house during odd hours of the night while armed with firearm weapon; committed rape with my daughter on gun point and due to his conduct under the heat of passion, impending danger at his hands I made firing upon his person under sudden and grave provocation. It was not a planned occurrence but occurred due to act of deceased Mujahid Hussain. During investigation I and my all co-accused persons as well as my daughter Memoona deposed this narration of occurrence which proved correct during two rounds of investigation. My daughter Memoona had died on 18.08.2023 and due to this reason she could not produce in re-investigation of this case. However, she made statement to the police on the very first visit of police at the spot and also in remaining investigation. I made firing upon the person of deceased just to save myself, my property and the lives of my family members as well as honour of my family. The FIR was lodged after due deliberation, consultation, negotiations and after preliminary inquiry while sitting in the police station with a considerable un-explained delay. All the story narrated by the complainant party about the occurrence is absolutely false and incorrect. Complainant and his witnesses had deposed falsely against me and my co-accused persons out of their close relationship with the deceased and just to save the blameworthy conduct of deceased Mujahid Hussain and to blackmail us. Neither the complainant nor his witnesses were present at the spot at the time of occurrence nor we had called the deceased from his house prior to the occurrence. During investigation discharge report of my co-accused Faisal was prepared which is Ex.DE. During re-investigation the complainant and his eye witnesses took special oath to the effect that neither my co-accused Faisal was present at the place of occurrence at the time of occurrence nor made firing upon the person of deceased and statements of complainant and his witness are Ex.DB and Ex.DD. Complainant also admitted during investigation that deceased had gone to the place of occurrence for commission of rape and Ex.DC is statement of complainant in this regard.”

The other five co-accused, namely, Waleed, Muhammad Yasir, Muhammad Faisal, Abdul Majeed and Rehana Kausar (since acquitted), had also deposed in line with the appellant’s statement, while recording their statements under section 342 Cr.P.C. It would not be out of place to mention here that as per Manzoor Ahmad SI Investigating Officer of the case (CW- 9), Mujahid Hussain (deceased) had a revolver in his hand which was taken into possession by him vide recovery memo (Ex-CW8/C) and according to woman Medical Officer Dr. Bushra Asghar (CW-6), Memona Bibi was brought for medical examination before her on 08.04.2023 at 02:30 p.m. and in her opinion, in view of medico legal findings and report of Punjab Forensic Science Agency (PFSA) sexual intercourse has been committed. The photographs of the dead body were prepared by Zahid Yaseen 1164/C at the spot which were taken into possession by the Investigating Officer of the case (CW-9), vide recovery memo (Ex-CW1/A), which showed that Mujahid Hussain (deceased), at the time of death was not wearing any shirt, so, there is hardly any doubt left with the fact that the deceased in fact had trespassed into the house of the appellant with a revolver for illicit purpose and thereby subjected his daughter to rape.

7. Before discussing the availability of ‘right of self defence’ to the appellant, keeping in view the given circumstances of the case, it would be advantageous to discuss the relevant provisions of law in this regard. Chapter IV of the Pakistan Penal Code, 1860 (PPC) relates to the GENERAL EXCEPTIONS and sections 96 to 106, deal to the right of private defence. Relevant provisions in this regard read as under;- 96. Things done in private defence: Nothing is an offence which is done in the exercise of the right of private defence.

97. Right of private defence of the body and of property: Every person has a right, subject to the restrictions contained in section 99, to defend- Firstly: His own body, and the body of any other person, against any offence affecting the human body;

Secondly: The property, whether moveable or immovable, of himself or of any other person, against any act which is an offence falling under the definition of theft, robbery, mischief or criminal trespass, or which is an attempt to commit theft, robbery, mischief or criminal trespass.

100. When the right of private defence of the body extends to causing death: The right of private defence of the body extends, under the restrictions mentioned in the last preceding section, to the voluntary causing of death or of any other harm to the assailant, if the offence which occasions the exercise of the right be of any of the descriptions hereinafter enumerated, namely:__ First: Such an assault as may reasonably cause the apprehension that death will otherwise be the consequence of such assault; Secondly: Such an assault as may reasonably cause the apprehension that grievous hurt will otherwise be the consequence of such assault;

Thirdly: An assault with the intention of committing rape; Fourthly: An assault with the intention of gratifying unnatural lust; Fifthly: An assault with the intention of kidnapping or abducting; Sixthly: An assault with the intention of wrongfully confining a person, under circumstances which may reasonably cause him to apprehend that he will be unable to have recourse to the public authorities for his release.
(underline has been provided for emphasis)

So, on going through these provisions of law, there is no ambiguity that every person has a right not only to defend his own body, but body of any other person against any offence affecting the human body and the right of private defence extends to protect a woman who has been assaulted with the illicit intention. I am mindful of the fact that in case when any accused takes a specific plea, the burden shifts upon the accused under Article 121 of the Qanun-e-Shahadat Order, 1984 (QSO), to prove his plea but there is hardly any cavil with the proposition that in that case, the accused’s burden would not be as heavy as that of the prosecution. Article 121 of the QSO, was obviously promulgated to relieve the prosecution from the necessity of proving the certain facts, which might bring the case within the general exceptions but in such case the Court should appraise the prosecution evidence and defence version in juxtaposition, in order to arrive at just conclusion. However, the prosecution would not absolve to prove its case as per basic theory ‘beyond reasonable doubt’ if the Court reaches to the conclusion that the accused could not discharge his liability. The august Supreme Court of Pakistan in case of “ALI AHMAD and another” had held that in case where the accused has taken a specific plea or produced evidence in his defence, the Court should appraise the prosecution case and defence version in juxtaposition in order to arrive at just conclusion. Even in such situation the burden remained on the prosecution to prove the necessary ingredients of the offence charged against the accused and it does not shift upon the accused merely by taking the defence plea or producing evidence in his defence and if the prosecution fails to prove its case against the accused, the question of shifting of burden on the accused does not arise. In case of “MAZHAR IQBAL and another”

it was observed that when the complainant and PWs have admitted that the deceased was maintaining illicit relations with a middle aged lady of 45 years and was also widow, the entry of the deceased to the house of accused was certainly not for any good reason, but for illicit purposes then how the accused could be convicted for such charges when all the facts and circumstances clearly told that the deceased had trespassed in the house for no other but for that purpose. The provisions of law give right to the occupant of any property to expel the intruder/trespasser and if the trespasser has made a trespass for illicit matters, then the right of self-defence of property and person is further fortified even to the extent of causing death of that trespasser. The Supreme Court of India in “YESHWANT RAO”

had observed that when the prosecution alleged that the sexual victim was a consenting party; the Supreme Court while elaborating the sections 96, 97 & 100 of the IPC (pari matria provisions with PPC) acknowledged the father’s right of private defence extending to cause death of the assailant and acquitted the appellant/accused from the charge of murder. In case of “ASHIQ ALI AHMAD and another v. The STATE and others (PLD 2020 Supreme Court 201) MAZHAR IQBAL and another v. The STATE and others (2017 SCMR 2036) Yeshwant Rao v. State of Madhya Pradesh (AIR 1992 SC 1683) HUSSAIN”

it was held that defence plea is to be considered in juxtaposition with the prosecution case and in final analysis, if the defence plea is proved or accepted true, the prosecution case would stand shattered and discarded. If defence plea is substantiated to the extent of creating doubt in the credibility of the prosecution witnesses, that would be enough but in case it is not established no benefit would accrue to the prosecution on that account, hence, its duty to prove the case ‘beyond reasonable doubt would not be diminished even if the defence plea is not proved or is found to be palpably false.

8. So, under the circumstances, I entertain no doubt in my mind that the learned trial Court travelled beyond the scope of law on the subject, wherein it was held that the appellant had exaggerated his right of self defence as the learned trial Court, in impugned judgment had disbelieved the prosecution version and found that the act of the appellant was defensive, hence, justified. It was then non-comprehendible that as to how the Court had branded the same as illegal or exaggerated the same. Even otherwise, when the Court had itself believed that right of self defence to accused was available but on going through the impugned judgment, I find that the learned trial Court did not clarify as to how that right has been exceeded. So, in that eventuality, I believe that the reasoning of learned trial Court proceeded on supposition and there is hardly any cavil with the well entrenched principle of Criminal Administration of Justice that suppositions were to be resolved in favour of the accused.

9. As discussed supra, since the learned trial Court itself had firmly declared that the prosecution evidence was not worthy of reliance and discredited the same, so, without looking it to the plea of the appellant, he has to be acquitted straightway. Even otherwise, the learned trial Court has also not advanced any ground or reasoning to hold his opinion that how the appellant had exaggerated his right of self defence, which was available to him under the law.
ASHIQ HUSSAIN v. The STATE (1993 SCMR 417)

10. The upshot of the above discussion is that there being no satisfactory basis to uphold conviction and sentence of the appellant awarded by the learned trial Court through impugned judgment, so in that eventuality, while allowing the instant appeal, the same are set aside and appellant, Abdul Waheed, is acquitted of the charge. He is in jail, be released forthwith, if not required to be detained in any other case.

11. So far as Criminal Revision No.41722 of 2025 for enhancement of sentence of the appellant/respondent No.1 filed by the complainant is concerned, since the prosecution has failed to prove its case against the appellant/respondent No.1 and has been acquitted from the case, therefore, this petition having no merits is dismissed accordingly.
(MUHAMMAD WAHEED KHAN)
JUDGE APPROVED FOR REPROTING JUDGE Sajid
